correctness.rationale: For each fixed Parikh vector the swap graph is bipartite by inversion parity. The first-unequal-designated-pair involution pairs every odd vertex to an even adjacent vertex, with fixed points necessarily even. This explicitly proves that the even side is maximum, independently of any experimental enumeration. Fixed point counts are exactly F(r), and summing unmatched words gives q^ceil(n/2); boundary n=1 is included. The included checker independently computes matching-based graph optima in 2, 3 and 4 symbol alphabets over the specified finite lengths.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the exact independent-set/detection capacity in all q-ary lengths and in every content class. The arXiv 2301.11680 and 2023 Khuat-Kim primary texts treat correcting adjacent swaps combined with edits, not the present weaker detection-only extremum. Abdel-Ghaffar 1998 concerns simultaneous substitution-and-transposition detection, a stronger admissibility requirement whose bounds do not imply the stated detection-only formula; its unavailable full text remains a concrete priority risk. Classical inversion q-multinomials determine the parity class sizes, but not the graph upper bound without the new matching argument. published-finding corpus searches returned related channel results but no logical covering theorem, under best-knowledge comparison.
residual_risks: Full text of the close 1998 joint-detection paper could not be inspected; it may contain transposition-only results not stated in the abstract.
Inversion-parity enumeration is classical; priority risk concerns whether the matching saturation statement was previously recorded under another graph-theoretic name.
No independent external validation has yet been performed.

value.rationale: Single adjacent symbol interchange is a natural human-entry and string-channel error, and maximum detectable code cardinality with no correction demand is its exact combinatorial coding capacity. The result determines this previously unlocated invariant simultaneously for all alphabets and all blocklengths, and refines it by every fixed content class (important in composition-constrained storage). The direct matching certificate exposes optimality rather than merely constructing a half-sized parity code. No downstream theorem is required and neither classical inversion parity alone nor computation alone is claimed as the contribution.
